<thought>Based on the ESI‑MS spectrum the most intense ion is at m/z 183.0451, which corresponds to the [M+H]⁺ ion. Subtracting the mass of a proton gives a neutral molecular mass of ≈182.0378 Da. The strong M+2 peak (~33 % of the base peak) indicates the presence of a single chlorine atom (⁷⁵Cl/³⁷Cl isotopic pattern). Removing the monoisotopic mass of ³⁵Cl (34.968852 Da) leaves 147.06896 Da to be accounted for by C, H and O atoms. A composition of C₆H₁₁O₄ matches this residual mass within ~3 mDa (≈18 ppm). The resulting formula C₆H₁₁O₄Cl gives a DBE of 1 (consistent with the observed isotopic pattern) and fits the observed M+1 intensity (~10 %). Therefore the most plausible molecular formula is C₆H₁₁O₄Cl. </thought>
<final_answer>C6H11O4Cl</final_answer>
